Source and verification code for the paper *Subexponential Weighted Counting and Exact Optimisation* by Deep Bhattacharjee.

The paper reproduces, with credit, the summation routine of OpenAI's preprint "The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False" (25 October 2026) for sparse formulas, and proves from it, with complete proofs, that the following are computed deterministically in time 2^{o(n)}: the whole weight profile of a sparse weighted constraint system (Max-k-SAT, Min-k-SAT, the count of optimal assignments), the number of satisfying assignments of each Hamming weight, Max-Cut and the maximum and minimum bisection of a sparse graph, the weighted independence polynomial of every graph (hence the independence and clique numbers and their counts), Vertex Cover in time 2^{o(k)} + poly(n), partition functions and homomorphism counts on bounded-degree graphs, the density of states of Ising and Potts systems with polynomially bounded couplings, dominating sets, matchings, hitting sets and sparse permanents, counting under a congruence, k-SAT in SE and SNP ⊆ SE.

Files: `subexponential-weighted-counting.pdf` (the paper), `subexponential-weighted-counting-tex.zip` (LaTeX source and figures), `subexponential-weighted-counting-arxiv.tar.gz` (arXiv-style source). The exact-arithmetic check program and its recorded output are in `code/`.
